messages:
maria: ran a ~15min nsys trace on the model that regressed at seqlen 4096. link: https://perfetto/reports/abc123 (goes to perfetto exported from nsys)

dave: nice, what stood out?

maria: HBM bandwidth flat near card peak for long stretches, then sudden 80-150ms gaps where throughput drops and KV eviction kernels spike. looks like periodic writeback contention.

maria: pasted the key snippet from the timeline (abbreviated):
```
00:12.341 fused_attn_forward        10.2ms
00:12.353 kv_read_span             48.7ms  <-- sustained
00:12.402 kv_evict_batch           120.4ms <-- eviction surge
00:12.523 cudaMemcpyAsync          5.1ms
```

kai: eviction batch 120ms is huge. is microbatching doing something weird? what’s our batching heuristic config for this run?

maria: default adaptive microbatch: target_latency_ms=40, max_microbatch=8, pad_strategy=auto. we increased prefetch window to 64 pages for this experiment.

song: try capping max_microbatch to 4 and reduce prefetch window to 32. also enable kernel affinity override so smaller kernels prefer SM-optimized path.

dave: can you paste the nsys CLI you used? want to reproduce locally.

maria: sure
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=cpu,context --output=run_2321112
```

maria: i also ran nvprof-like counters via CUPTI to capture dram_util and dram_read_throughput.

perf-bot: automated note: trace uploaded to perf-storage at s3://redwood-traces/2321112223/run_2321112.nsys

kai: if HBM is fully saturated then eviction writes could be competing with read streams. maybe our KV writeback is synchronous in certain codepaths — look for any host->device syncs near kv_evict_batch.

maria: saw a few `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` inside the eviction cleanup when slab_count > 1024. patching that out reduced tail-latency in a small run.

dave: good find. another angle: kernel selection - the runtime sometimes picks the "small-matmul" kernel for attention at seq len 4096 because of heuristics tied to token distribution. force the large-matmul kernel to see if it improves overlapped bandwidth.

song: add a quick experiment: 1) cap microbatch 4, 2) patch out sync, 3) set KERNEL_PREFERENCE=large_matmul. run nsys for 3 min and compare HBM occupancy and nvtx regions.

maria: queued that. initial 3-min result: avg dram_read 520GB/s vs 690GB/s before, eviction stalls almost disappeared, p50 latency down ~18%.

kai: interesting that avg dropped — probably because we blocked pathological read amplification. do we have perfetto flamegraph of kernel lifetimes?

maria: uploaded a perfetto slice: https://perfetto/viewer/xyz789. timeline shows more consistent kernel overlap instead of long serial kv_read + evict sequences.

dave: assign a follow-up: add unit test for slab_count branch that caused sync, and update batching heuristic to back off prefetch when evict writeback backlog > 1. I'll file a PR.

maria: thanks — i'll attach the nsys trace and the condensed timeline to the PR. also leaving the run metadata in the trace S3 path.

perf-bot: PR created: #4278 by dave - "kv: avoid sync in eviction; backoff prefetch when writeback backlog high" :thumbsup:

maria: nice. next step: run a canary on a dedicated node to validate throughput cost impact before pushing to main cluster.

song: can we add an eval prompt set that exercises long-seq behavior so we catch regressions in CI? small checklist on the PR would be helpful.

maria: will add tests and the perf artifact links in the PR description.

maria: tl;dr: root cause was twofold — sync in eviction path + prefetch window too aggressive causing writeback contention; mitigation by limiting microbatch and forcing alternative matmul kernel improved latency and reduced HBM spikes.
